# Question 1

## i

For this question, the weighted integral statement is, 
$$
\int_0^L w(x)\left[ \frac{d}{dx}\left(EA\frac{du}{dx}\right) + b(x) \right]  \, dx = 0
$$ {#eq-weighted-integral-statement}

## ii

Expand the bracket in the @eq-weighted-integral-statement, 
$$
\overbrace{\int_0^L w(x)\left[ \frac{d}{dx}\left(EA\frac{du}{dx}\right)\right]dx}^{I} +\int_0^L w(x)b(x)   \, dx = 0
$$

We try to end up with the same continuity requirement between $u(x)$ and $w(x)$

-   u(x): must at least be twice differentiable (because we have $\frac{d}{dx}\left(EA\frac{du}{dx}\right)$)
-   w(x): No differentiability requirement (because we have w(x))

Apply integrating $I$ by parts,

$$
\left(w(x)EA\frac{du}{dx}\right]_0^L-\int_0^LEA\frac{dw}{dx}\frac{du}{dx}dx+\int_0^L w(x)b(x)dx=0
$$

Expand the natural B.C.
$$
w(L)EA\frac{du}{dx}\bigg|_L-w(0)EA\frac{du}{dx}\bigg|_0-\int_0^LEA\frac{dw}{dx}\frac{du}{dx}dx+\int_0^L w(x)b(x)dx=0
$$
Boundary term for this problem,

- Case 1: Dis appears when we have an essential B.C, at x=0, u=0, so we impose w=0
- Case 2: At $x=L, EA\frac{du}{dx}=2EA_0\frac{du}{dx}=F$

$$
w(L)EA\frac{du}{dx}\bigg|_L-\int_0^LEA\frac{dw}{dx}\frac{du}{dx}dx+\int_0^L w(x)b(x)dx=0
$$

Given that: 𝐸 =100 GPa, 𝐴0 =0.005 m2 𝐹 =100 N and 𝐿=1 m
